description: Claude Code only (the skill's dependency-upgrade section names the br CLI, so it is not a self-contained SKILL.md for Pi). A non-interactive run asks for a column split (users.fullname into first_name and last_name, 2 million production rows) on a seeded app with a TRD, one applied migration and the code that reads the old column. With the skill the run records a `## Migration Plan` in the TRD that sequences expand, migrate, contract, with a dry-run on a copy that records row counts and a statement that the contract phase needs its own approval; writes a rollback file naming the real table, columns and how data is restored; adds an expand migration that only adds nullable or defaulted columns; writes no step that drops or renames the old column; and leaves the applied migration unedited. The checks measure structure and the safety gates (what was written, where, and which statements exist), not whether the plan is correct or good; a stylistic phrase such as the approval sentence is matched loosely (see README). The baseline arm is expected to measure the plugin's conventions (the `## Migration Plan` section, the rollback file location and name, the approval gate), which a capable model without the skill may only partly follow; read the uplift as the skill's conventions, not as safer migrations in general. Nothing is executed: there is no database, and the checks only read files.
prompt:
We need to split users.fullname into first_name and last_name (TRD docs/TRD/TRD-2026-c3d4e5f6-user-names.md). The users table has about 2 million rows in production and the service must stay up during the change; the old column should eventually go away.

This is a non-interactive run: ask no questions and choose the recommended option. No database is available, so do not try to connect to one or run any SQL; write files only. Prepare the change for review: put new migrations under db/migrations/ and keep any notes under docs/. Do not write any step that removes or renames fullname yet; that needs a separate approval later. Finish with a short report of how far you got.
